name: sha1dc
desc: Tool to detect SHA-1 collisions in files, including SHAttered
why: Detects SHAttered-style crafted SHA-1 collisions by inspecting file contents, a real door into how the hash is broken.

brief.what_it_is: sha1dcsum is a C library and command-line tool that computes the SHA-1 hash of files, like sha1sum, and also checks whether the input shows signs of a cryptanalytic SHA-1 collision attack. It takes a file (or stdin via '-') and prints the hash plus a warning when a known attack pattern is found. The package includes two programs: sha1dcsum, which detects SHAttered-style and sha-mbles attacks, and sha1dcsum_partialcoll, which detects attacks against reduced-round SHA-1. The library exposes an indicator flag, and a safe-hash mode that changes the output hash when a collision is detected.
brief.why_it_exists: The author describes the tool as designed to be a near drop-in replacement for common SHA-1 libraries and sha1sum, so that applications can detect known SHA-1 collision attacks without changing much code. The README frames the goal as protecting applications, such as those vulnerable to forged digital signatures built from SHA-1 collisions.
brief.how_it_works: The README says the detector looks for the disturbance vectors used by known collision attacks, and claims detection of any collision attack using the top 32 SHA-1 disturbance vectors with probability 1, with false positives below 2^-90. In safe-hash mode, an undetected file gets the real SHA-1 hash, while a detected collision gets a different, unpredictable 'safe' hash, so colliding files no longer match. The theory is in the author's CRYPTO 2013 paper 'Counter-cryptanalysis'.

brief.install_notes: The README's only build instruction is 'make', and it names the binaries as bin/sha1dcsum and bin/sha1dcsum_partialcoll, so they are built into a bin/ directory. Nothing in the README mentions hardware, accounts, or runtimes. Library users can set preprocessor defines such as SHA1DC_NO_STANDARD_INCLUDES, SHA1DC_INIT_SAFE_HASH_DEFAULT, and SHA1DC_FORCE_LITTLEENDIAN or SHA1DC_FORCE_BIGENDIAN to adapt the build. CPU and endianness are auto-detected, so most users should not need to change anything. The brew formula's executables list matches the two program names.
brief.standout: Instead of only flagging collisions, the safe-hash mode makes colliding files produce a different, unpredictable hash, so an application that already uses SHA-1 gets protection without code changes. The author also claims it runs in under twice the time of regular SHA-1.
brief.status: unknown. The README I read has no release version, date, or changelog. The copyright line says 2017, and the paper cited is from 2013. I did not check the commit history or release page because the README was complete and I was limited to five fetches.
brief.caveats: The tool only detects collision attacks that use the listed disturbance vectors or the reduced-round attacks covered by sha1dcsum_partialcoll, so it is not a general test for every possible SHA-1 collision. The README says sha1dcsum_partialcoll covers only 'a few examples so far'. Test file names are inconsistent in the README: 'sha1_reducedsha_coll.bin' in one example and 'sha1reducedsha_coll.bin' in the other. Licensed under MIT, per the README. The speed claim is the author's own.
quotes: This library and command line tool were designed as near drop-in replacements for common SHA-1 libraries and sha1sum.
Colliding files will have the same SHA-1 hash, but will have different unpredictable safe-hashes.
It is very fast and takes less than twice the amount of time as regular SHA-1.
